brief.title: The Ninth Bell
brief.premise: A bell-founder's apprentice in a fog-drowned estuary city hears the storm-bells ring a pattern no founder cast, and the parish orders the bells silenced before the next fog.
constraints: Lit by gas and oil only; no electrical devices.

world.name: Bellwether
world.description: A gas-lit estuary city where nine bronze storm-bells on the sea-wall hold back the Chiming, a fog that steals the names of anyone it hears spoken.

locations.name: The Sea-Wall Belfry
locations.description: The great wall mounting the nine storm-bells that ring the fog back.

locations.name: Founder Row
locations.description: The foundry street where every bell was cast and struck with its maker's mark.

locations.name: The Fogmarket
locations.description: A licensed night market that opens only in fog, where names and secrets are traded.

locations.name: Bailiff's Stairs
locations.description: The steps up to the parish court where the watch's writs are read.

locations.name: The Salt Chapel
locations.description: The chapel where every citizen's name is written on salt and kept against the fog.

factions.name: The Founder Collegium
factions.description: The collegium of bell-founders who cast, tune and answer for every bell on the wall.

factions.name: The Parish Watch
factions.description: The wardens who keep the silence laws and can still a bell by writ.

factions.name: The Fog Brokers
factions.description: Licensed traders in names and secrets who work the Fogmarket under charter.

rules.statement: The wall mounts nine bells and no more; casting a tenth is treason against the parish.
In fog, a spoken name belongs to the fog; citizens carry name-tokens and answer to signs.
Every bell is struck with its founder's mark, and its ring can be traced back to the caster.
Every citizen's name is registered on salt at the chapel; an unregistered name is forfeit to the fog.

history.name: The Raising of the Wall
history.description: Nine bells were cast and mounted on the sea-wall to hold the Chiming at bay.

history.name: The Lost Parish
history.description: In a fog that lasted nine nights, a whole parish forgot its names; the salt registry was founded in answer.

history.name: The Brokers' Charter
history.description: Trading in names was licensed and confined to the Fogmarket to keep it out of the parlours.

conflicts.name: The Tenth Ring
conflicts.description: An unmarked tenth bell has been heard in the pattern; the founders deny casting it and the watch wants the bells stilled.

conflicts.name: The Name Debts
conflicts.description: Fog brokers hold name-debts over half the parish; the watch calls it extortion, the brokers call it charter.

characters.name: Elsa Quill
characters.description: A bell-founder's apprentice on Founder Row who can read a casting flaw at a glance and hears the wall's bells like voices.
characters.motivation: To prove the tenth ring was cast by a human hand and clear the collegium.
characters.goal: Trace the unmarked ring to its caster before the bells are stilled.
characters.flaw: She trusts craft rules too completely to see when they are being weaponised.
characters.internal_conflict: If the caster is not a founder, everything she was taught about marks is wrong.
characters.external_conflict: The parish watch has the writ to silence the wall and the will to use it.

abilities.name: Ring-sight
abilities.description: Reads a bell's casting flaws and its founder's mark from its ring.

characters.arc: Elsa learns that a mark is a signature, and signatures can be forged.

characters.name: Warden Hale
characters.description: The parish warden who signed the silence writ, whose own watch cast the unmarked bell to justify quietening the wall.
characters.motivation: To still the bells, which he believes trade safety for superstition.
characters.goal: Silence the wall before the next fog, whatever it takes.
characters.flaw: He has made an end so just that no means can shame him.
characters.internal_conflict: He knows the fog is real but fears the bells' hold on the parish more.
characters.external_conflict: Elsa's ring-sight can prove the unmarked casting was the watch's work.

abilities.name: Writ authority
abilities.description: Moves writs through the parish court faster than anyone can answer them.

characters.arc: Hale's own unmarked bell tolls his confession.

characters.name: Tallow
characters.description: A fog broker who trades in names from a licensed stall and knows which name the tenth bell was cast for.
characters.motivation: To sell what he knows before the fog calls in his own name-debt.
characters.goal: Trade the ringer's true name for his own safe passage.
characters.internal_conflict: Selling the name betrays the only client who ever paid fair.
characters.external_conflict: Both the watch and the founders would take the name without paying.

abilities.name: Name-keeping
abilities.description: Keeps a bought name safe in memory through any fog.

characters.arc: Tallow sells the truth cheap, for once, and buys back his name.

relationships.description: Tallow sells Elsa the clue to the unmarked bell's caster.
relationships.conflict: His price is a name-token she is sworn to protect.

relationships.description: Hale's silence writ is aimed at the wall Elsa maintains.
relationships.conflict: He rings the very treason he accuses the founders of.

storyboard.title: The Ninth Bell
storyboard.logline: A founder's apprentice proves the parish watch cast the unmarked bell it cites to silence the wall.

scenes.title: The Unmarked Ring
scenes.summary: On the Sea-Wall Belfry, Elsa hears a tenth ring in the pattern and reads no founder's mark in it.
scenes.conflict: An unmarked bell is either treason or forgery.
scenes.outcome: Elsa certifies the ring is bronze, cast by a skilled hand off the Row.

scenes.title: The Silence Writ
scenes.summary: At Bailiff's Stairs, Warden Hale reads a writ stilling the bells, citing the unmarked ring as proof the founders broke charter.
scenes.conflict: The writ is lawful unless the ring can be traced.
scenes.outcome: Elsa wins three days to trace the caster before the bells are stilled.

scenes.title: The Broker's Price
scenes.summary: In the Fogmarket, Tallow sells Elsa a casting-mark rubbing found in the fog, priced in name-tokens.
scenes.goal: Buy the clue to the caster.
scenes.conflict: The price is a name she is sworn to protect.
scenes.outcome: She pays her own token; the rubbing bears the watch's foundry stamp.

scenes.title: The Salt Register
scenes.summary: At the Salt Chapel, the registry shows the ringer's name was never salted: someone the fog could not report.
scenes.conflict: An unsalted name is proof and sacrilege at once.
scenes.outcome: The gap in the registry matches the watch's own bell-keeper.

scenes.title: The Watch's Bell
scenes.summary: On the wall, Elsa strikes the impounded tenth bell and reads its flaws aloud: it was cast in the watch's own foundry to fake a founder's treason.
scenes.goal: Prove the forgery before the court.
scenes.conflict: Hale's writ stands unless the proof rings true.
scenes.outcome: The mark is read; Hale's writ is void and his bell is condemned.

scenes.title: The Answered Chiming
scenes.summary: The false bell is melted, the nine ring the next fog back over the wall, and Elsa's own mark is struck on the recast bronze.
scenes.conflict: The parish must trust the bells again after learning they can be forged.
scenes.outcome: The Chiming is answered; Bellwether keeps its names.

evidence_summary: The world, cast and storyboard satisfy the brief's gas-lit storm-bell setting; deterministic validators are clean and there are no blocking defects.
